Noah: Hey all - onboarding question: I'm about to open my first PR that tweaks router debounce and adds a tiny unit test. Any team norms I should follow (branch name, commit message, reviewers, PR size etiquette)?

Harper: Welcome Noah! Our lightweight norm: keep a PR per logical change. If router logic + its tests are a single behavior change, one PR is fine. If you touch public configs or generated code, split into schema/gen PR then usage PR.

Lina: Branch names we use: `task/<TICKET>-short` (we've been experimenting with `task/` instead of `feature/`). Commit style: `area(scope): short summary` e.g., `router(debounce): reduce duplicate calls`. Include ticket in branch and PR title.

Noah: Any hard LOC limits or perf sign-off rules?

Harper: No hard rule, but prefer under ~400 LOC of product code. If test fixtures inflate the diff, note that in PR body. For changes that could affect latency, add `needs-perf` label and mention @review-squad. We do a perf quick-check (p50/p95) for risky changes.

lint-bot: Pre-commit hooks configured: black, isort, mypy, flake8. CI will block merges on failing hooks. Run: `pre-commit run --all-files`. CI: https://ci.redwood.example/job/2012345678

Noah: Example git flow?

Lina: TL;DR:```bash
git checkout -b task/ENG-987-small-debounce
make test  # runs unit tests locally
pre-commit run --all-files
git add -A && git commit -m "router(debounce): reduce noise on cold start"
git push --set-upstream origin task/ENG-987-small-debounce
```

Noah: PR template? Rollback plan expectations?

Harper: Use the repo PR template. Minimal required sections: description, test plan (how to run tests locally), rollback steps (1-2 bullets), and perf notes if applicable. Example rollback: "revert PR -> redeploy -> run `tools/cachectl purge --prefix=router:`".

Lina: Reviewers: add one CODEOWNER for the path + one peer. If CODEOWNERS requires approval, that's the gate. Label it `area/runtime` and `needs-review`. For flaky CI mark `flake` and ping @eng-oncall.

Noah: Merge strategy? Squash or preserve history?

Harper: Squash for small fixes is fine. For multi-commit features keep commits and use the PR description to explain the steps. If you're unsure, choose squash and mention it in the PR.

Noah: Any gotchas (generated files, large binaries)?

Lina: Don't commit generated outputs from `gen/` unless you changed the generator. Run `scripts/generate.sh` locally if you touched schema. Use `git add -p` to avoid accidental big diffs.

Noah: Great, thanks! I'll open the PR and drop the link. Appreciate the quick triage :)

review-squad: Happy to review when you post the link. If you want a quick pair-review, tag me and we'll hop on a quick call.
